steps.action: Launch a new grain through the app's first action, "Open compliance workspace", and open it as the grain owner. The grain root redirects itself to /setup; no path is typed by hand.
steps.expectedResult: The grain serves the page titled "Open a Compliance Workspace — DueProcess", with the heading "Open a Compliance Workspace" and a sticky banner reading "NETWORK UNVERIFIED — no network declared by the configuration owner. Do NOT assume this is a test network.". No deployment artifact in this package sets MELUSINA_NETWORK, so an undeclared network is the state a fresh grain launches in, and the banner must say so rather than describe the chain as simulated — a banner reading "TEST MODE — Simulated network" (the pre-B08.6 default) is a FAILURE of this probe. It is served with a normal success status: no 403, no blank iframe, no supervisor reset. A fresh grain has never had a package selected, so the first-launch gate redirects every path except /setup, /static/* and /api/*.

steps.action: Read the whole first screen and look for a case list, case queue, Kanban board, or any case data.
steps.expectedResult: There is none, and that absence is the pass condition. The page offers exactly two cards and nothing else: "Activate a Compliance Procedure" (button "Pick a Procedure...") and "Configure a Custom Procedure" (button "Define Custom Procedure"). This release ships no embedded domain catalogue — the DomainTemplate grain is the sole publisher of definitions — so a fresh grain that reaches a dashboard, a Kanban board, or any named procedure would mean an unsigned definition was activated locally, and is a FAILURE of this probe.

steps.action: Reload the grain from the shell. Do not click "Define Custom Procedure": that POSTs /api/setup/blank and would configure the grain out of its fresh state.
steps.expectedResult: The same "Open a Compliance Workspace" setup screen renders again. The unconfigured state is read back from the grain's own persisted store — no package-selection record and an empty flow store, logged as "flowstore: no templates — station is unconfigured (bind to Template grain)" — rather than being a first-paint race that would later settle into a dashboard.

steps.action: Launch a second grain through the app's other action, "Open new case", and open it as the grain owner.
steps.expectedResult: The page titled "New Case — Setup Needed" renders, reading "This is a DueProcess Compliance process grain. It is waiting for a DueProcess Compliance Station grain to push a workflow template over Grapple before a case can be opened.", followed by "Operator steps to wire it up". The page is terminal by design and carries no link, button, or form: a process grain cannot open a case until a Station pushes it a signed template.

steps.action: From a popaye client account, submit the KYB profile so the Station spawns an account-opening case, then read the merchant's landing page.
steps.expectedResult: The merchant shows a real case reference instead of 'case pending creation'. Before this release the spawn aborted on 'record process initial context ... execution_mode="delegated"; canonical integration evidence requires internal execution', so the caseID never reached the client even though the case existed and was Active on the Station dashboard.

launchProbe.expectedResult: Both of the app's actions launch on a fresh grain and render their own explicit, human-readable unconfigured state under enforced authz. Neither invents a workflow definition locally. Reaching case data on a fresh grain would prove the retired embedded-template bypass had returned, and fails the probe.

steps: Delete the probe grains created for the launch probe; each is a fresh grain created solely for this probe.
No external state is created: the probe never advances past the unconfigured setup screen, so no case, no template binding, and no sidecar record exists to retract.
No sidecar is contacted and no lease is minted, so nothing is retained off-grain. All probe state lives in the deleted grains' own /var.
